newsitem.title: USA: Firms unveil ways to ease Internet jams.
newsitem.headline: Firms unveil ways to ease Internet jams.

text.p: Two computer network hardware companies Monday announced technologies to ease congestion on the Internet, a problem some experts have warned could lead to a Net "meltdown."
Cisco Systems Inc. introduced a tagging system that would give some Internet traffic priority over other, putting it into a fast lane on the information highway.

Cisco also unveiled a high-powered switch for Internet backbones -- the "trunk lines" of the globe-spanning network of computer networks -- and improved router equipment. Routers transmit information and switches direct it.
Separately, Ascend Communications Inc. introduced a high-powered switch for Internet backbones.
However, these technologies could hurt the Internet's egalitarian nature, with those who can pay getting better service and a better Internet experience from Internet service providers analysts said.

"That is definitely coming, that is what the ISPs (Internet service providers) are talking about to (raise) quailty of service," said analyst Eric Hindin of the Yankee Group. "There will be a variety of pricing mechanisms: one type for consumers and another for corporate users."
Cisco's "Tag Switching" technology offers Internet service providers a way to offer differentiated service, Cisco and analysts said, something akin to overnight mail vs. first-class mail.

The technology works by assigning a tag to traffic at points where it enters the overall Internet traffic flow. The software then gives routers and switches on the Net the ability to read tags on the traffic indicating their priority.
The technology will help the backbones, "which are being stressed by the exponential growth of Internet and (internal corporate) intranet traffic," Cisco said in a statement.
"There is a big interest in handling multimedia and voice," said product spokesman Steve Bauer "To do that, you have to better manage and tune the traffic through the network."

Cisco also unveiled its high-powered StrataCom BPX switch, which integrates two new technologies known as asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) and frame relay. The switch is among the first major products to come out of the merger of Cisco and Stratacom Inc., the company said.
It is four times as fast as the predecessor StrataCom switch it is based on.
Ascend announced a high-performance Internet switch it said was designed to solve the congestion problem on Net backbones.
Ascend said its GRF Series switches are designed to replace routers in the Internet backbone networks.
Hindin said Yankee Group believes one of the biggest needs to ease Internet congestion is to replace the routers in backbones with switches, a more heavy-duty way to move information.
Jim Diestal, who represents backbone provider Pacific Bell said, "We should see some opportunity to bring some congestion control further out in the network to (Internet service providers)."
To date, most Internet service providers have charged a flat fee based on a set number of hours per month of access to the Internet.

But to pay for the equipment needed to increase capacity at various points of the Internet, service providers will need to charge premium fees to generate sufficient profits without losing the mass market customer, who generally doesn't want to pay more than $19.95 a month.
